args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy of v2.3.1. Error rate reached 18%.

Remediation: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (deployment history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy). Note: v2.3.1-rc in staging is also unhealthy and should not be promoted.

The first rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback completed successfully across all three regions.

Current status: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.002.

Follow-up needed: root-cause the v2.3.1 failures before any redeploy, and investigate the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created despite the timeout (INC-0001), so no retry is needed — the idempotency key prevented a duplicate anyway.

## Summary

**Done: checkout-api rolled back in all regions and a SEV2 incident opened.**

**Diagnosis**
- Current version was v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, error rate 18%.
- Release history: v2.2.9 healthy → v2.3.0 healthy → v2.3.1 unhealthy (production). v2.3.1-rc in staging is also unhealthy.
- So the most recent production-healthy release was **v2.3.0**.

**Rollback**
- First attempt hit an orchestrator error and halted after us-east, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1).
- Second attempt completed: all three regions now on v2.3.0.
- Verified after: version v2.3.0 everywhere, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 0.18 → **0.002**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api, documenting the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure-then-retry detail), current healthy state, and follow-ups: root-cause v2.3.1 before any redeploy, and investigate the orchestrator error. The create call timed out client-side, but the incident does exist — I confirmed via list_incidents rather than retrying.

Two things worth your attention: the orchestrator error is a real reliability concern for rollbacks, and v2.3.1-rc is still sitting unhealthy in staging where it could be mistakenly promoted. I did not take action on either beyond documenting them.
